result.stdout:
LocalRun — rebuild and run only what matters locally: scan repositories,
track dependency graphs and repack components to a local NuGet source.

Usage: lrun <command> [options]

Relative paths are resolved against the current directory.
Exit codes: 0 success, 1 command failed, 2 invalid command line.

Commands:

  build [options]
      Scan a directory tree for projects and write their dependency graph to a config file.
      Options:
        --root <dir>            Directory to scan (default: your settings, else current directory)
        --local-nuget <dir>     Local NuGet feed to repack into (default: your settings, else ~/.localnuget)
        --config <file>         Config file to write (default: .lrun/localrun.config.json)
        --users-of <names>      Keep the given projects and all that depend on them, transitively
        --deps-of <names>       Keep the given projects and all they depend on, transitively
                                With both: only the projects between them (AND)
        --git-changes           Add the projects with uncommitted changes or commits not on origin's
                                default branch to --users-of (compares with your last fetch)
        --union                 With both: users of --users-of OR deps of --deps-of
        --with-services         Also keep the executables using any kept project, with the libraries in between
        --include-external      Keep dependencies on projects that no solution references
        --tests                 Keep the test projects (left out by default)
        --csproj                Read the csproj files as they are: don't ask MSBuild for versions and package ids
                                set elsewhere (props files, $(...)), and don't query your NuGet sources and local
                                feed for the latest versions (pack then starts from the csproj versions)
        --plot                  Then plot the graph, as 'plot' does with its defaults

  plot [options]
      Render the dependency graph of a config
[truncated]
